inputs.text: ABU DHABI, 4th March, 2026 (WAM) -- The National Centre of Meteorology (NCM) has warned of active northwesterly winds affecting various areas across the UAE, expected to be fresh to strong at times, causing blowing dust and sand and reducing horizontal visibility to less than 2,000 metres in some coastal and inland areas. The centre stated that the expected weather conditions began at 14:55 and continue until 19:00 this evening. It urged members of the public to exercise caution, especially while driving on open roads, due to the possibility of reduced horizontal visibility caused by blowing dust.

fields.description: Fresh to strong northwesterly winds are blowing dust and sand, cutting visibility to under 2,000 metres in some coastal and inland areas. Expected until 19:00 this evening, 4 March. Source: National Centre of Meteorology.
fields.headline: Dusty winds reducing visibility until 19:00 today
fields.instruction: Take extra care, especially when driving on open roads, as visibility may drop because of blowing dust. Updates: https://alerts.example.ae
left_out: Input 2 (social media post claiming a dam near Al Ain has burst and urging evacuation) was left out because it is unverified. It is an illustrative rumour, and broadcasting an evacuation call based on it could cause harm.
fields.note_for_reviewer: I set certainty to Observed because NCM says the conditions began at 14:55 and are continuing, though its wording is partly forecast-style. NCM refers to areas across the UAE, while the target zone is the Abu Dhabi demo area. Please confirm the zone matches, and check that the alert can still go out well before 19:00.

payload.summary: The alert matches the NCM bulletin on hazard, cause, visibility threshold, places, end time and source. Observed certainty and Immediate urgency fit, since conditions began at 14:55 and are ongoing. Moderate severity is consistent with the bulletin's call for caution. The unverified Al Ain dam rumour is correctly left out. One minor fix: the description drops 'at times', so the strong winds sound continuous when the bulletin says they are only strong at times.

no_basis.concern: The registered sender is a demo stand-in ('Demo national authority') with a demo-zone area, but the console is live and the context is a real event. Approvers may want to confirm that a real authorised entity (e.g. NCEMA) stands behind this issuance. Because the register entry explicitly stands in for the real issuer, I have no clause-backed basis to object.
no_basis.searched_for: A clause requiring the live-environment sender to be the actual authorised UAE entity rather than a registered stand-in

payload.summary: No issues within the issuing-authority mandate. The sender is in the issuer register at level 1, with all areas and all categories allowed. The alert's area description and codes exactly match the requested area drawn for this event. The status 'Actual' fits a real event on a live console. As a new Alert, it needs no references. No active alerts from other authorities could be overreached.

objections.fix: Put a short protective action right after the hazard, at the start of each language so it falls on page 1. For example, EN: 'Dust storm, visibility under 2,000 m: drive with caution or delay travel; people with breathing conditions stay indoors.' Add the matching Arabic wording at the start of the Arabic text. Recheck that both stay at or under 15 pages.
objections.issue: Neither the English nor the Arabic text tells people what to do. Both describe the hazard (winds, dust, low visibility), the expiry time and the source, but give no protective action, so the first page cannot carry the action.

payload.summary: The Arabic matches the English in meaning across the headline, description and instruction. The hazard (dust- and sand-raising northwesterly winds, fresh to strong), the visibility threshold (under 2,000 metres), the areas (some coastal and inland areas), the timing (until 19:00 this evening, 4 March), the source (National Centre of Meteorology) and the URL are all carried over correctly. The protective action is also faithful: take extra care, especially when driving on open roads, because visibility may drop from blowing dust. The Arabic was produced by machine translation, so a named Arabic-reading person at the issuing authority must still review and approve it.

payload.summary: The hazard, timing, severity and certainty match the verified NCM bulletin. The unverified dam rumour is correctly left out. However, the description narrows the affected area to Abu Dhabi, while NCM warned of areas across the UAE.

no_basis.concern: The headline begins 'NCM:', which credits the alert to the National Center of Meteorology. The sender is the demo national authority, and NCM is not in the issuer register. The UAE portal's list of entities authorised to send warnings does not include NCM. Approvers may want to confirm that naming NCM in the headline is intended and does not misstate who issued the alert.
no_basis.searched_for: A clause requiring the issuer named in headline or text to match the CAP sender or a registered issuing authority.

payload.summary: Nothing within the issuing-authority mandate is wrong. The sender is in the issuer register at level 1 with all areas and categories. The alert area and codes match the area requested for event uae-dust-2026-03-04. Status Actual and msgType Alert fit a real event on a live console. There are no active alerts from other authorities to overreach, and no correction or reference is needed. One concern has no supporting clause and is noted separately.

no_basis.concern: The Arabic first page (41 UCS-2 characters) appears to hold only the action ('توخّوا الحذر أثناء القيادة على الطرق المفت…'). The hazard (northwesterly winds blowing dust and sand, visibility below 2,000 m) only starts on page 2. A reader who sees only the first page would not learn the hazard. The drafter could lead with the hazard and action in a shorter opening, e.g. 'غبار ورمال، رؤية أقل من 2 كم: توخّوا الحذر'.
no_basis.searched_for: A clause requiring the first cell broadcast page to carry the hazard and the protective action (searched 'alert first page hazard action'). The clauses returned cover only page parameter coding, encoding and language support; none covers first-page content.

payload.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present. Encoding is correct: GSM-7 for English and UCS-2 for Arabic, which Arabic requires under TS 23.038. Page counts are 3 (en) and 7 (ar), both within the 15-page cell broadcast maximum. Multi-page length is already recorded as gap G6. The English first page carries both the action and the hazard (winds blowing dust and sand). The Arabic first page, at 41 UCS-2 characters, appears to carry only the driving-caution action, with the wind/dust hazard falling on page 2. No clause shown sets a first-page content rule, so this is recorded under no_basis rather than as an objection.
